items.title: Democrats Ask Musk to Preserve Documents on Starlink in Ukraine

items.content: <article>Democrats on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee have asked SpaceX Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk to “preserve all documents, communications and electronically stored information” related to the company’s Starlink and Starshield systems in Ukraine,” according to a letter released Friday.</article>

items.title: All Airports Are Ground Stopped Until Further Notice: FAA
items.content: <article>"Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Ray LaHood, former US Transportation Secretary, says he believes the nationwide FAA ground stop is more likely the result of an old, antiquated system failing than problems transitioning to new technology. LaHood says travelers should consider alternate plans because disruptions could continue even after the system is restored, and says major airports are prepared to handle the fallout. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump to Hold Trilateral Meeting With Xi, Putin in China

items.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Jensen’s Nvidia Departure
items.content:
<article>The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF

After weeks spent denying the allegations of infidelity and fighting to remain in his job as Nvidia’s chief executive officer, Jensen Huang’s surrender late Wednesday night was unconditional. His usual take-charge demeanor had evaporated, according to a person familiar with the situation, and he’d started using phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.” Huang’s admittance to an affair with an alleged spy has had an international ripple effect across the AI and tech industry.

On today’s episode:

Ian King, Bloomberg News US Semiconductors Reporter
Cat Barton, Bloomberg News Seoul Bureau Chief
Joe Wiesenthal, Bloomberg ‘Odd Lots’ Podcast Co-Host
Mark Jacobson, International Spy Museum Historian (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: LaHood Says Antiquated FAA System Likely Failed
items.content: <article>Ray LaHood, former US Transportation Secretary, says he believes the nationwide FAA ground stop is more likely the result of an old, antiquated system failing than problems transitioning to new technology. LaHood says travelers should consider alternate plans because disruptions could continue even after the system is restored, and says major airports are prepared to handle the fallout. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.author: Tim Balk

items.title: Ground Stop Fix Will 'Take Some Time,' Mullin Says
items.content:
<article>Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says it will take some time to resolve issues affecting flights around the country. All flights have been grounded. He can't rule out the reason is a cyber attack, but he says travelers are safe. 
“It’s going to take some time, and so this isn’t going to just be resolved and turned around within the hour. This is going to take take some time,” he told reporters at the White House on Friday.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Hungary Finds $20 Million Cash in Probe of Orban Minister
items.author: Thomas Escritt and Andras Gergely
items.content: <article>Investigators have found nearly $20 million worth of cash hidden in forests, barns and warehouses across Hungary, a breakthrough in the widening probes into alleged corruption by allies of former Premier Viktor Orban.</article>

items.title: Jensen Huang Scandal Fallout Grows
items.content: <article>A Chinese company founded by Alice Huang, the woman at the center of a controversy dogging Nvidia, procured smuggled AI chips that were installed at a Shanghai data center with links to Megaspeed International, according to documents reviewed by Bloomberg News. Bloomberg News Seoul Bureau Chief Cat Barton takes an international view of Jensen Huang’s downfall. Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter Ian King also brings an exclusive inside look at Huang’s final hours as Nvidia CEO. Plus, Bloomberg News Technology Reporter Matt Day has the update and fallout of Microsoft’s massive services outage. Finally, Lis Agosto, Director of Product Research & Strategy at Global X ETFs, takes an investor’s view on the Nvidia scandal. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump Administration Lets States Delay New Medicaid Work Rules
items.author: Rachel Cohrs Zhang
items.content: <article>The Trump administration will let states delay a requirement that some people in the Medicaid program work, volunteer or go to school to get health insurance, pausing a controversial policy that would throw millions of people’s health coverage into question.</article>

items.content: <article>Bloomberg’s Sarah Foster joins Tom Keene on “Bloomberg Money.” By the numbers, Americans have never been richer.
